status_summary: The Ensuring Accurate and Complete Abortion Data Reporting Act of 2025 was introduced in both chambers on 2025-01-22 (H.R. 627, referred to Energy and Commerce, and S. 178, referred to Finance); it would make certain Medicaid family planning payments depend on annual state abortion data submissions to CDC. CDC's surveillance page (updated November 2024) says state reporting is voluntary with no national requirement. In September 2025 a public radio outlet reported an unsigned CDC email saying CDC was pausing analysis and would not release an abortion surveillance report, and in December 2025 CNN reported the annual report was delayed until spring 2026, with HHS and a former CDC official giving different explanations. An advocacy news site reported in July 2026 that no report on 2023 data had appeared and that the CDC director nominee called abortion surveillance critical. The GovInfo bill status records for both bills show 2025-01-22 as the latest action, with H.R. 627 having seven cosponsors and S. 178 eleven.

timeline.event: Ensuring Accurate and Complete Abortion Data Reporting Act of 2025 introduced in the House as H.R. 627 and referred to Energy and Commerce; Senate companion S. 178 introduced the same day and referred to Finance. Both bill status records show no later action.

CDC told Virginia vital statistics staff, in an unsigned email obtained through a state public records request, that it was pausing abortion data analysis and would not release an abortion surveillance report (the email's own date is not given; dated by the report that first described it).

CDC's annual abortion surveillance report, normally published in late November, had not been released and was delayed until spring 2026; HHS attributed the halt to a former CDC official's direction to return state data, which that official disputed (decision date not given; dated by the report).

title: Require states to report abortion data to CDC and pass the abortion data reporting bill

Press reports differ on why the report was delayed.
